authorship: Expected values written by hand by Claude (architect), checked independently with exact fractions, committed by Avi. Codex must never edit this file. If a case fails and you believe the expected value is wrong, stop and report the case ID and your reasoning.

interface.errors: Uses SeriesError and CoverageError from engine.series. Bad arguments raise the built-in ValueError.
interface.to_gbp(asset, fx): Returns a new MonthlySeries: asset values divided by the dollars-per-pound rate for each month both cover, labelled GBP, asset name and basis kept.
interface.currency_split(asset, fx, start, end): Returns a dict with exactly the keys local_return, currency_return, gbp_return for the period from month-end start to month-end end.

cases.derivation: Divide dollars by dollars-per-pound: 100/1.25 = 80, 100/1.00 = 100, 110/1.00 = 110, 121/1.10 = 110. Name and basis kept, labelled GBP.

The stock is flat in dollars (100 to 100). The pound falls from 1.25 to 1.00 dollars: -20% for the pound, but the dollar gains 1.25/1.00 - 1 = +25% against the pound. $100 was worth 80 pounds and is now worth 100 pounds: +25%. Check: 1.00 x 1.25 = 1.25.
Stock +10% in dollars (100 to 110), rate unchanged at 1.00, so +10% in pounds too.

Stock +10% in dollars (110 to 121). The pound strengthens from 1.00 to 1.10, so the dollar loses 1.00/1.10 - 1 = -1/11 = -9.0909...%. In pounds: 110 to 110, flat. Check: 1.10 x 10/11 = 1. The stock's gain was wiped out by the stronger pound.
U2 starts in 2019-11 but the rate starts in 2020-01, so the pound series starts in 2020-01. Same values as C01. Earlier dollar history is dropped, never converted at a guessed rate.
The asset covers 2019-12 but the rate does not. Not covered.
Same period and values as C05; the extra dollar history before 2020-01 changes nothing.
Conversion keeps the asset's basis: a price-only series stays price-only.
The asset is already in pounds. Only USD assets are converted.
The rate series must be labelled fx_rate.
The rate series must be dollars per pound, labelled USD.
An exchange rate is not an asset to convert.
The asset (2021) and the rate (2020) share no months.
Start must be earlier than end.
No split for an asset already priced in pounds.
